old: These functions can be assigned to a planner, worker and critic.
new: These functions can be assigned to a planner, implementer and reviewer.
reason: Aligns the introductory role names with the executed planner/implementer/reviewer labels used throughout the architecture.

old: It separates obtaining a program from the model from checking its correctness.
new: It separates program generation from correctness checking.
reason: Fixes an awkward and ambiguous construction while preserving the intended generation-versus-verification distinction.

old: Each condition receives the same supplied task/context and the same subsequent evaluator.
new: Each condition receives the same task and supplied context and is evaluated by the same subsequent procedure.
reason: Makes the controlled inputs and common evaluation procedure explicit and idiomatic.

old: A full response/program/report/resource archive, supplemented by 400 separate development programs, 199 programs from an INoT adaptation and a limited native repository-patch demonstration.
new: A complete archive of responses, programs, reports and resource records, supplemented by 400 separate development programs, 199 programs from an INoT adaptation and a limited native repository-patch demonstration.
reason: Improves idiomatic English and renders the revised Russian list of archived evidence more precisely.

old: The added value is an audit-focused replication and extension:
new: The added value is a verification-focused replication and extension:
reason: Matches the revised emphasis on inspectable executable evidence without implying a separate audit study.

old: On 79 control-eligible tasks, role differences are 0.00 and -1.27 points (both Holm $p=1$); valuation ratios are 0.990 and 1.000, with intervals crossing no difference.
new: On 79 control-eligible tasks, role-minus-neutral quality differences are 0.00 and -1.27 percentage points (both Holm $p=1$); valuation ratios are 0.990 and 1.000, with intervals that include zero.
reason: Names the contrast and unit explicitly and uses standard statistical English for intervals containing no difference.

old: An assignment is a planned generation for a specified task, condition and repetition; an assignment that has started counts as an attempt.
new: An assignment denotes a planned generation for a specified task, condition and repetition; once started, it counts as an attempt.
reason: Clarifies the protocol definition and removes a repetitive construction without changing the counting rule.

new: The task source is BigCodeBench v0.1.4~\cite{zhuo2024bigcodebench}.
reason: Makes clear that BigCodeBench is the source of the tasks, not the source of the experimental protocol.

old: The instruction-only model processes never receive these evaluator artifacts.
new: The generation processes never receive these evaluator artifacts.
reason: Matches the revised Russian scope: no generation process receives evaluator materials; the original wording unnecessarily narrows the claim to instruction-only processing.

old: The primary series' 18.45\% lower single-call role valuation is therefore not convincingly reproduced by this additional wording-and-layout experiment.
new: The primary series' 18.45\% lower single-call role valuation is therefore not convincingly reproduced under the changed wording and layouts in this additional experiment.
reason: Aligns the comparison with the revised Russian qualification that both wording and layout changed, without making a stronger cross-study claim.

old: Output serialization limits the interpretation of this negative result.
new: Patch-serialization errors limit the interpretation of this negative result.
reason: States the observed source of the limitation directly and matches the revised Russian wording.

old: The independent 80-task extension further limits the resource interpretation.
new: The independent 80-task extension further constrains the resource interpretation.
reason: Uses the more precise editorial verb for evidence that narrows generalization rather than merely reducing interpretation.
